source: measured on hardware by this project
_readme: Counter maxima measured by this project, layered on top of the upstream layouts in
data/reinkpy/counters.json. Kept in a separate file so regenerating those from reinkpy
Upstream declares a max for only 2 of 626 counters, so percentages otherwise cannot be
shown at all. Each entry here was derived by reading the printer and comparing against a
tool that reports percentages: max = value / (percent/100).
A second, stronger basis needs no reference tool at all: a printer declaring the pad at end
of life has reached its limit, so the counter value IS the maximum. Those entries record
"observed": { "value": N, "at": "service required" } and a range of one integer.
Only add an entry you have actually measured. Record the observation alongside it so the
figure can be re-checked, and note the range when the source's rounding leaves one — a
percentage printed to two decimals brackets the maximum, it does not pin it. Trailing zeros
in "percent" are deliberate: 60.90 says the tool was read to two decimals, and 60.9 does not.
Entries come from the app's Calibrate percentages card (db/Calibration.kt derives the maximum
and the range) and are merged with tools/apply_calibration.py, which checks them against the
layouts. A user overlay (counters-overlay.json) still wins over anything here.

calibrations.note: Pairing assumes the reference percentages come back in the same address order the counters are declared in. Maxima are model constants (pad capacity), not per-unit, so they apply across these SKUs. Deliberately NOT extended to the other 119 models sharing this EEPROM layout (ET-1810..ET-4800, L1210..L5318): a shared layout does not prove identical pad capacity.
